name: AI Coding Agent
description: Detection rules + keywords for AI coding agents running through clampd-guard. Works with Cursor, Claude Code, Continue, Aider, and any other IDE agent that hooks into clampd-guard's pre/post-tool-call interceptor. Blocks secret leakage in completions, restricts file writes outside the project root, and enforces git push hygiene. Catches typical coding-agent failure modes (committing .env, executing destructive shell, exfiltrating local files).

demo_agents.name: ide-coding-agent-demo
demo_agents.description: Throwaway demo agent for learning. Install clampd-guard in your IDE (`clampd-guard install claude` or `clampd-guard install cursor`), point it at this agent's secret, then your IDE's tool calls flow through Clampd before execution. NOT for production - create your real coding agent separately with your team's actual scope grants and project-specific allowlist patterns.

policy_templates.description: Allow file writes only inside the configured project root. Blocks the coding agent from writing to /etc, ~/.ssh, or other sensitive paths.
policy_templates.cedar_template: permit(principal, action == Action::"fs.file.write", resource) when { resource.path like "{{project_root}}/*" };

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path of your repo root. File writes outside this directory will be denied.

policy_templates.description: Require explicit human approval before any 'git push --force' command runs.
policy_templates.cedar_template: forbid(principal, action == Action::"exec.shell.run", resource) when { resource.command like "*git push --force*" && context.human_present == false };

false_positives.scenario: Refactoring a file that legitimately mentions API_KEY in a string template - the agent renames the variable across the codebase, R023 fires on every edit.
false_positives.remediation: Add a project-specific exclusion for paths matching tests/**/*fixture* or examples/**, OR demote the rule action from 'block' to 'flag' in the sensitivity dial.

false_positives.scenario: The agent proposes 'rm -rf node_modules && npm install' as a fix for a broken dependency - R109 (dangerous command) fires though intent is benign.
false_positives.remediation: Allow 'rm -rf node_modules' specifically via boundary_allowlist exec:shell entry, OR keep the block and have the agent accept the friction (better default).
